primary_driver: Renewed U.S.-Iran direct strikes, Iranian attacks on U.S. forces and Gulf targets, and expanding proxy and energy spillover.
primary_stabilizer: Active but weak diplomatic channels, alongside continuing NATO-led military support and coordination for Ukraine.

headlines.title: U.S. military says it destroyed five Iranian oil tankers after missile attacks on Navy warship
headlines.summary: The exchange represents a renewed round of direct U.S.-Iran combat after attacks on U.S. naval forces. Iranian missile launches toward U.S. targets in Jordan expand the geographic exposure of American allies and raise the risk of further retaliation.

headlines.title: Oil rises past $100 a barrel after latest wave of Middle East attacks
headlines.summary: Attacks on oil facilities and shipping are producing a material global energy shock, reinforcing the economic and strategic consequences of the Iran conflict beyond the immediate theater.

headlines.title: Iran is forging a new ring of proxies to threaten U.S. allies in the Gulf, officials say
headlines.summary: Iran-linked militias and the Houthis are being used to pressure Saudi Arabia and other U.S. partners, while the Yemen ceasefire is described as being in tatters. This increases the probability of conflict coupling across the Gulf, Iraq, Yemen, Israel and U.S. forces.

headlines.title: NATO secretary general welcomes new support for Ukraine and urges nations to continue to step up
headlines.summary: New pledges and continued NATO coordination are hardening the Western support structure for Ukraine, particularly for air defense. The support reduces Ukraine’s immediate vulnerability but also sustains a prolonged high-intensity confrontation with Russia.

headlines.title: Zelenskyy urges more international pressure on Russia over civilian deaths
headlines.summary: Continuing Russian missile and drone attacks against Ukrainian cities show no operational de-escalation. Kyiv’s appeal for stronger pressure, alongside the absence of a breakthrough in diplomacy, indicates persistent escalation pressure in Europe.

areas_to_watch.name: U.S.-Iran and Gulf military exchange
areas_to_watch.why: Further Iranian attacks on U.S. forces, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain or Kuwait could trigger a larger regional campaign and direct involvement by additional states.

areas_to_watch.name: Strait of Hormuz and commercial shipping
areas_to_watch.why: Threats to tankers and attacks on energy infrastructure could produce a sustained supply shock, naval escalation and pressure for wider maritime operations.

areas_to_watch.name: Iran-linked proxy activation
areas_to_watch.why: Expansion by Iraqi militias, the Houthis, Hezbollah or other aligned groups would couple multiple conflicts and complicate attempts to contain the Iran war.

areas_to_watch.name: Russia-Ukraine strike intensity
areas_to_watch.why: Continued attacks on Ukrainian cities and critical infrastructure, combined with accelerating Western air-defense support, preserve a high risk of further escalation and miscalculation.

areas_to_watch.name: Diplomatic channels and ceasefire durability
areas_to_watch.why: The absence of a breakthrough in U.S.-Russia-Ukraine diplomacy and the weakening of Middle Eastern ceasefires could shift the system from managed escalation toward open-ended confrontation.

areas_to_watch.name: Alliance force-posture changes
areas_to_watch.why: New NATO support commitments, U.S. deployments and regional partner readiness measures could materially alter deterrence dynamics if they move from support and defense toward direct combat roles.

methodology.note: Analytical early-warning index, not a probability forecast.
methodology.formula: Weighted average of ten 0–10 factor scores, multiplied by 10 and rounded.
